mnemonic: A cross-shaped stem stuck into a round apple.
Two eels swimming side by side. "i" sounds like the "ee" in eel.
Someone doubled over after a punch to the stomach: "oof!"
An egret with a feather on its head, striding along.
A round-bellied golfer whose ball flies off to the right: "oh no!"
A blade slicing down with a chip flying off: a karate chop.
An old-fashioned key with two teeth.
An open beak calling "coo, coo".
A keg standing on the left with its tap handle on the right.
Two short cords lying flat, one above the other.
A fish hooked on a line: salmon for supper.
A fishing hook lowered into the water. She caught one.
A curly straw for sipping soup.
A wide mouth with one fang showing: set your teeth.
A zigzag stitch: sew it up.
The letters t and a squeezed together spell "ta".
A cheerleader with one arm up and a round pom-pom.
A wave curling over: a tsunami.
A hand cupped to catch something. "Te" is the Japanese word for hand.
A toe with a thorn stuck in it.
A cross above a tied loop: a nautical knot.
A bent knee beside two lines for the shin.
Tangled noodles with a little loop at the end.
A cat curled beside a post with its tail in a loop. "Neko" is Japanese for cat.
A no-entry sign: a circle with a slash.
A fence post and someone with arms out, laughing "ha ha".
A wide grin: "hee hee".
Mount Fuji with snow sliding down both sides.
A low hill. "Hey, that's an easy climb."
A post beside a chimney with two bars of smoke. Santa says "ho ho".
A ship's mast with two crossbars. "Mama, look at the ship!"
A looping musical note: do, re, mi.
A cow's face with a ring in its nose: "moo".
An eye with crossing lashes. "Me" is the Japanese word for eye.
A fishing hook with two bars: catch more fish.
A yak's head with one horn and one ear.
A fish swimming round in a U-turn.
A yo-yo dangling on its string.
A rabbit sitting up, seen from the side, with one ear.
Two reeds swaying by the river.
A winding route that ends in a loop.
A post with a line that kicks out to the right: relax and stretch a leg.
A winding road with no loop at the end.
A post with a big round belly, like a wasp's body.
Someone wading into water: "whoa, it's cold!"
It looks like a handwritten letter n.
An axe with a bent handle.
An easel leaning on its leg.
A woodpecker's head with a crest on top.
A steel girder, the kind an engineer builds with.
A dancer kicking one leg out: "oh, nice move!"
Hiragana か without the flying chip: a clean karate chop.
Hiragana き without the bottom curve: a simpler key.
A cook's tall hat seen from the side.
A letter K that has tipped over.
Two corners making three sides of a box.
A gate with a sagging right post.
Two drops stacked on the left and a stroke sweeping up from the bottom. She looks sideways.
A hanger with a suit sliding off it.
Hiragana せ with sharp corners: set your teeth again.
One drop and a long stroke falling from the top. So it falls.
Katakana ク with an extra dash: a talon gripping a twig.
The cheerleader again, now with straight arms.
Two drops along the top and a stroke falling from above, like a tsunami crashing down.
A telephone pole with two crossbars.
A totem pole with one arm pointing.
A knife cutting across a line. "Naifu" is Japanese for knife.
Two lines. "Ni" is the Japanese word for two.
Crossed chopsticks picking up noodles.
A tree with its roots showing. "Ne" is the Japanese word for root.
A single slash: half of the no-entry sign.
The two sloping sides of a hat.
A heel seen from the side.
A flag caught by the wind: "foosh".
The same hill as hiragana へ. "Hey, they match."
A holy cross with a spark on each side.
An arrowhead pointing down at a spot on the map.
Three missiles in flight.
A cow's nose from the side: "moo".
An X on the target: aim with your eye. "Me" means eye.
Hiragana も with straight strokes: still catching more fish.
Hiragana や without the ear: a simpler yak.
A U-boat from the side: hull below, tower on top.
A comb with three teeth. "Yo, nice hair."
A ramen bowl with its lid floating above.
The same two reeds as hiragana り, standing straighter.
Two roots spreading out under a tree.
A lever pulled up to the right. The Japanese r sits between r and l.
A square room.
A water glass with one side missing.
Katakana フ with an extra bar: "whoa, one more line".
One drop and a stroke rising from the bottom, like シ with a drop missing: the end.
